review_candidates.description: Re-Generate – Australia. Re-Generate is a specialist engineering consultancy delivering mechanical design, project and asset support to the hydropower and water sectors. This is a specialist assessment role with real value add, the work you do will directly inform upgrade, repair and risk-mitigation decisions on critical, high-value plant, in a business that encourages initiative and supports its people to deliver practical, high-quality solutions. The role You'll evaluate the structural integrity for critical hydropower and water assets: building and validating complex FEA models, running Fitness-for-Service assessments against API 579-1/ASME FFS-1 and BS 7910, and turning the results into pragmatic remediation strategies that balance safety with keeping plant running. You'll be equally comfortable deep in a non-linear model, on site interpreting inspection data, or explaining what it all means to a client who has a decision to make. Because the Australian branch is still getting established, this role is remote. Expect regular travel to client sites across the east coast of Australia, plus periodic trips to our NZ head office to work closely with the engineering team there as necessary. »         What you'll be doing: –        Developing, running, and validating complex Finite Element Analysis (FEA) models to evaluate stress, strain and remaining life of structures and components –        Conducting Fitness-for-Service (FFS) assessments of flaws and defects in accordance with API 579-1/ASME FFS-1, BS 7910 and relevant Australian/New Zealand standards –        Determining remediation strategies that balance safety with operational continuity, drawing on current site inspection and NDE/NDT data. –        Performing seismic stability modelling and hydrodynamic pressure calculations to applicable standards –        Undertaking Fluid-Structure Interaction (FSI) analysis, combining CFD and FEA, to assess flow-induced vibration and support fatigue and fracture assessments –        Leading forensic investigations of structural and mechanical failures — identifying root cause and providing pragmatic, innovative solutions. –        Building 3D models in SolidWorks (or similar) to support analysis and decision making –        Producing calculations and reports that are clearly documented for peer review, and working towards Check/Approve authority under our Design Office Handbook –        Liaising with the different technical teams (predominantly the asset integrity team) in NZ for support and guidance as required. About you You're a Mechanical Engineer specialising in FEA and Asset Integrity work who is at home in the detail — you know the standards, you understand what the numbers mean physically, but your pragmatic and understand the model is only as good as the site validated. You take initiative without needing to be told what to do next, and you're comfortable working in a business that's still writing parts of its playbook. Just as importantly, you can bring people with you. You write reports that turn dense technical content into clear, concise messages a client can act on, you collaborate well with, sub-contractors and suppliers, and you promote confidence in Re-Generate's capability every time you're in front of an external party. You'll bring: »         A bachelor’s degree in mechanical or Materials Engineering — a Master's or PhD in Solid Mechanics / Fracture Mechanics is highly regarded. »         6+ years' dedicated experience in structural integrity, advanced stress analysis, and fracture mechanics »         A proven record performing FFS assessments and non-linear FEA on rotating and stationary assets, ideally in power generation. »         Detailed working knowledge of API 579-1/ASME FFS-1, BS 7910 and AS/NZS 1170; familiarity with AS 4100 and AS 1210 (or equivalents) advantageous »         The ability to interpret NDE/NDT results and integrate them into structural integrity models. »         A sound knowledge of hydro processes and systems — desirable »         CPEng status with Engineers Australia, or actively working towards it; RPEQ registration highly advantageous. »         Strong technical report writing and constructive communication skills. »         The adaptability to thrive in a small consulting business, and the initiative to improve things as you go. »         Willingness to travel regularly, including to remote sites and to New Zealand. Why Re-Generate You'll have genuine autonomy over your technical work and a direct line of sight from your analysis to the decisions clients make, supported by an experienced Australian Manager, the NZ engineering team, and a business that trusts capable people to get on with the job. As the branch grows, so does the opportunity to shape how integrity assessment is done here.

review_candidates.title: Lead Engineer - Civil, Structural and Geotechnical Works
review_candidates.description: Somebody has to close the loop between the ground study and the layout We usually know a great deal about the ground before engineering starts. The investigation has been done and the report exists. What is not guaranteed is that the manufacturer’s engineers design to it, or that what they hand back finds its way into the layout. Somebody has to close that loop. Ground study into supplier design, supplier design back into the layout, and then every consequence that follows for piling, drainage, access and cable routes. Closing it is the job. Technica works as EPC-M contractor on utility-scale solar, wind and battery storage projects across Europe, currently including a ground-mount solar farm of around 130 MW in Ireland. On the ground and structures side you would scope the geotechnical investigation, specify the pile test regime and interrogate what comes back, then hold the substructure suppliers to it: their foundation design, their mechanical design for it, module mounting and installation tolerances, and the structural review of inverter and MV station foundations and substation civils. On the works side you would own earthworks and grading, drainage and surface water management, access tracks, haul and crane routes, trench design and cable route civils, fencing and boundary works, temporary works, and the planning and permitting conditions that constrain all of it. The detailed design of foundations and structures sits with consultants and suppliers. Your job is to define what they need to deliver, to judge whether the result is actually buildable, and to hold the line when a layout optimisation quietly creates a drainage or an access problem. The interfaces are where this role earns its keep. Cable routes, station positions and duct runs are electrical and control decisions that land in your drawings. Your grading and drainage decisions land back in theirs. If you enjoy that negotiation, you will enjoy this role. If you would rather receive a frozen layout and design to it, you will not. This role is hard in specific ways, and we would rather say so now: -  You will have to get a supplier’s engineering team to engage properly with a ground report they would rather apply their standard solution to. That is as much a persuasion problem as a technical one. -  Merging a revised foundation design back into a layout means reopening work that other disciplines already consider finished, and being the person who asks for that. -  You will have to say no to layout changes that look free and are not. -  A real part of the week goes into drawing review, registers and comment sheets. -  The role involves being on site, in weather, at the moments when it matters. At Technica you will join a young, fast-growing company working across photovoltaic, wind and battery energy storage projects throughout Europe. We are part of the renewable energy transition, but we are not here to write reports about it from a distance. We develop projects, solve problems, take responsibility and move things forward. You will work directly with senior decision-makers, clients, utilities, suppliers and experienced project teams. Short decision paths, real ownership, and no expectation that you stay inside the lane your job title suggests. If you also have strength in electrical works or control systems, there is room here to use it rather than hand it off. You may come from civil or structural consultancy, EPC or contracting, infrastructure, geotechnical engineering, ports, roads, wind foundations or heavy industrial construction. Mechanical engineers who have worked on steel structures and installation methodology are equally relevant. Solar experience is welcome and not required. What matters is that you have designed or reviewed groundworks and structures that were then actually built, and that you went back and saw what happened. Candidates would typically have something like seven to ten years of engineering experience behind them. That is a centre of gravity, not a cut-off. If you can do the work, we are not going to count years. The role can be based in Ikast, Køge (Copenhagen) or Athlone. Remote work is possible as much as reasonable for the role and project needs. The role involves travel to project sites and to external design partners in Europe: not constant, but real. Our working language is English. Danish is useful and not required. Apply via the link on this page with a short introduction and your CV. And tell us about a time the ground did not behave the way the design assumed, and what it cost.
